# Unblot

> Unblot is a free, anonymous poetry platform. Anyone can publish a poem without a byline, read
> work from other writers, and respond with likes and comments. Every poem is credited only to
> "Anonymous", so readers judge the writing rather than the writer.

Site: https://www.unblot.app

## Key facts

- **Cost:** Free. No paid tier, no submission fees, no charge to keep work on the site.
- **Account:** Required only to publish, comment, or like. Reading is fully open and needs no sign-in.
- **Attribution:** Poems display no author name, handle, or avatar. All work is published as Anonymous.
- **Rights:** Writers keep full copyright and can edit or delete their poems at any time.
- **Content:** Open-form and multilingual — free verse, spoken word, short lyric poems, and structured forms.
- **Discovery:** Poems are tagged and searchable; daily writing prompts seed themed work.
- **Trending:** Ranks recent poems by likes, comments and views over a recent window, so new work can surface.

## Pages

- [Latest poems](https://www.unblot.app/): Newest anonymous poems published to the public feed.
- [All poems](https://www.unblot.app/poems): Complete archive of every published poem, newest first, paginated.
- [About and FAQ](https://www.unblot.app/about): What Unblot is, how anonymity works, rights, and how to publish.
- [Trending](https://www.unblot.app/trending): Poems with the most reader engagement recently.
- [Discover](https://www.unblot.app/discover): Full-text search across titles, poem text, and tags.
- [Collections](https://www.unblot.app/collections): Curated groupings of poems.

## For crawlers

- Individual poems live at `https://www.unblot.app/poem/<slug>-<uuid>` and are server-rendered:
  the full poem text, publication date, tags, and schema.org/Poem structured data are present in the
  initial HTML response without executing JavaScript.
- A live sitemap is available at https://www.unblot.app/sitemap.xml
- Crawl permissions are declared at https://www.unblot.app/robots.txt

## Citation

Poems are the copyright of their authors, who publish anonymously. When quoting a poem, cite the
poem title and its Unblot URL. Do not attribute a named author — none is recorded.
